topics: 🙌 Blessings of Seeing — the mishna's list: sites of miracles, uprooted idolatry, storms, mountains, the great sea
🌧️ Good and Bad Tidings — HaTov veHaMeitiv, the True Judge, Sheheḥeyanu, and blessing for bad as for good
🚫 Vain Prayer — praying over what already happened; two prayers on entering a city, Ben Azzai's four
🏛️ Reverence for the Temple — the eastern gate, staff and shoes, shortcuts, 'from everlasting to everlasting', greeting in God's name
🦁 Miracles for an Individual — Jethro's blessing, the man saved from a lion, Mar son of Ravina's spring and camel
🗺️ Sites of Miracles — the Arnon and the lepers Et and Hev, the stones of Elgavish, Og's mountain, Lot's wife, Jericho's wall
🚢 Four Who Must Give Thanks — Psalm 107, thanking before ten with two Sages, and Rav Yehuda's recovery

overview.title: 📖 Overview: Blessings for What One Sees and Survives
overview.subtitle: Berakhot 54a–54b
overview.hebrewSource: חַיָּיב אָדָם לְבָרֵךְ עַל הָרָעָה כְּשֵׁם שֶׁמְּבָרֵךְ עַל הַטּוֹבָה
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: A new chapter opens with one long mishna of blessings triggered by experience rather than by the clock: seeing a place of miracles, a storm, the great sea, hearing good or bad news, building a house. It adds the rule that one blesses for the bad as for the good, derived from 'with all your heart, soul, and might', and closes with laws of reverence for the Temple and two enactments of the Sages. The Gemara derives the blessing over miracles from Jethro, shows that individuals bless over their own miracles, walks through a baraita's list of miracle sites with the midrash behind each, and ends with Rav Yehuda's four who must give thanks — seafarers, desert travelers, the healed, and the freed prisoner.

slides.title: 🙌 The Mishna's Blessings, Trigger by Trigger
slides.subtitle: What one sees or hears, and what one says
rows: A place where miracles were done for Israel
שֶׁעָשָׂה נִסִּים לַאֲבוֹתֵינוּ בַּמָּקוֹם הַזֶּה — Who performed miracles for our forefathers in this place
A place from which idolatry was uprooted
Who eradicated idolatry from our land
שֶׁכֹּחוֹ וּגְבוּרָתוֹ מָלֵא עוֹלָם — Whose strength and power fill the world
The great sea (Rabbi Yehuda), when seen only occasionally
הַטּוֹב וְהַמֵּטִיב — Who is good and does good
A new house or new vessels
שֶׁהֶחֱיָינוּ — Who has given us life, sustained us, and brought us to this time

callout.label: Source for a blessing on miracles:
callout.text: Rabbi Yoḥanan: 'And Jethro said: Blessed be the Lord, Who delivered you out of the hand of the Egyptians' (Exodus 18:10).

slides.title: 🌧️ Bless for the Bad, Do Not Pray for the Past
slides.subtitle: Three more rulings from the mishna, and its Temple-related laws

boxes.title: Vain prayer
items: Crying out over the past is a vain prayer (תְּפִלַּת שָׁוְא)
His wife is pregnant and he prays 'may she bear a boy'
He hears a scream in the city and prays 'may it not be from my house'

boxes.title: Entering a city
items: Two prayers: on entering and on leaving
Ben Azzai: four — two on entering, two on leaving
He gives thanks for the past and cries out for the future

boxes.title: Bless for bad as for good
items: 'With all your heart' — with both inclinations, good and evil
'With all your soul' — even if He takes your soul
'With all your might' — with all your money; or: for every measure He metes out to you, thank Him

callout.label: Temple reverence and two enactments:
callout.text: No levity facing the eastern gate, aligned with the Holy of Holies; no entering the Temple Mount with staff, shoes, money belt, or dust on one's feet; no shortcut through it, and spitting all the more so. Temple blessings ended 'until everlasting'; when the heretics claimed there is only one world, the Sages instituted 'from everlasting to everlasting'. They also enacted greeting a friend with God's name, as Boaz did (Ruth 2:4) — 'It is time to work for the Lord; they have made void Your Torah' (Psalms 119:126).

slides.title: 🦁 Does an Individual Bless Over His Own Miracle?
slides.subtitle: The mishna speaks of Israel's miracles; the Gemara tests the private case

nodes.content: ❓ For a miracle of the many we bless — but for a miracle of an individual we do not?
🦁 A man walking by the Euphrates was attacked by a lion and miraculously saved. Rava told him: whenever you reach that spot, bless 'Who performed a miracle for me in this place'.
💧 Mar son of Ravina, thirsty in a valley of willows, had a spring created for him. Later in the market of Meḥoza a wild camel attacked; a wall split open and he took shelter.
🔁 At the willows he blessed 'Who did a miracle for me in the willows and with the camel'; at Meḥoza, 'with the camel and in the willows'.

columns.label: Miracle of an individual
columns.content: He alone is obligated to bless

slides.title: 🗺️ The Baraita's Tour of Miracle Sites
slides.subtitle: Each place on the list comes with a verse or a midrash

steps.content: 1️⃣ Crossings of the sea and of the Jordan — explicit verses (Exodus 14:22; Joshua 3:17)

2️⃣ Streams of Arnon — 'Vahev in Sufa' (Numbers 21:14): Emorites hid in caves to ambush Israel; the Ark flattened the mountains, crushing them; the lepers Et and Hev saw the blood flowing and Israel sang
3️⃣ Stones of Elgavish — stones that stopped 'because of a man' (Moses, when the hail ceased) and fell 'because of a man' (Joshua, at the descent of Beit Ḥoron)

4️⃣ Og's rock — he uprooted a mountain three parasangs wide to hurl at Israel's camp; God sent grasshoppers to bore through it and it fell on his neck; his teeth grew out and held it ('You lengthened the teeth of the wicked', Reish Lakish on Psalms 3:8); Moses, ten cubits tall, leapt ten cubits with a ten-cubit axe and struck his ankle
5️⃣ The rock Moses sat on (Exodus 17:12); Lot's wife — a tragedy, so one says 'the true Judge', and for Lot 'Who remembers the righteous', for even in His anger God remembered Abraham (Genesis 19:29)
6️⃣ Jericho's wall 'swallowed in its place' — the verse says it fell, but since its width equaled its height, merely falling would have changed nothing; it sank

slides.title: 🚢 Four Who Must Give Thanks
slides.subtitle: Rav Yehuda's list from Psalm 107, and how the thanksgiving is to be said

lines.speaker: Rav Yehuda
lines.text: In Rav's name: four must give thanks — seafarers, desert travelers, one who was sick and recovered, and one released from prison. Each is in Psalm 107: they cry to the Lord in their trouble, He delivers them, and 'they thank the Lord for His kindness'.

lines.speaker: Rav Yehuda
lines.text: The blessing: בָּרוּךְ גּוֹמֵל חֲסָדִים טוֹבִים — Blessed is He Who bestows good kindnesses.

lines.speaker: Abaye
lines.text: And he must give thanks before ten, for 'let them exalt Him in the congregation of the people' (Psalms 107:32).

lines.speaker: Mar Zutra
lines.text: And two of them must be Sages: 'and praise Him in the assembly of elders'.

lines.speaker: Rav Ashi
lines.text: Say all of them must be Sages! — The verse says 'congregation of the people', not 'of elders'. Then say ten ordinary people plus two Sages! — The difficulty stands.

lines.speaker: Story
lines.text: Rav Yehuda fell ill and recovered. Rav Ḥana of Baghdad and the Sages said: 'Blessed is the Merciful Who gave you to us and not to the dust.' He replied: you have exempted me. There were ten present, and he answered amen — which counts as blessing himself.

callout.label: Rav Yehuda's other lists:
callout.text: Three need protection: the sick, a bridegroom, and a bride (a baraita adds a woman in childbirth; some add a mourner, and Torah scholars at night). Three things that, prolonged, lengthen one's days: prayer, the meal at one's table, and time in the bathroom — and the Gemara immediately asks whether prolonging prayer is really a virtue.

summary.principle: One is obligated to bless for the bad as for the good, and to thank God for miracles and rescues — publicly, before ten, when one has been delivered from sea, desert, sickness, or prison.

flowSteps.content: 🙌 Mishna: blessings on seeing miracle sites, uprooted idolatry, storms, mountains, the great sea; good and bad tidings; new house
🚫 Prayer over the past is vain; bless for bad as for good — 'with all your heart, soul, and might'; reverence for the Temple
🦁 Jethro's blessing is the source; Rava and Mar son of Ravina show that an individual blesses on his own miracle, at that place

columns.content: 🗺️ Miracle sites: Arnon, Elgavish, Og's mountain, Moses' rock, Lot's wife (True Judge + Remembers the righteous), Jericho
🚢 Four give thanks (Psalm 107): 'Who bestows good kindnesses', before ten, two of them Sages

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: A miracle for the many obligates everyone; a miracle for an individual obligates him — and answering amen to others' thanks fulfills it

quiz.q: According to the mishna, which of the following is a 'vain prayer'?
o: Praying on entering a dangerous city
Praying that one's pregnant wife will give birth to a boy
Reciting a blessing over bad tidings
Thanking God for the past upon leaving a city
quiz.e: The mishna gives two examples of crying out over the past: praying about the sex of a child already conceived, and praying that a scream already heard in the city is not from one's own house.

quiz.q: How does the mishna derive that one must bless for the bad as for the good?
o: From Jethro's blessing after the Exodus
From 'with all your might' — with every measure that He metes out to you, thank Him
From Boaz greeting the harvesters
From Psalm 107
quiz.e: The mishna expounds Deuteronomy 6:5: 'with all your heart' (both inclinations), 'with all your soul' (even if He takes your soul), 'with all your might' (all your money, or alternatively, every measure God metes out).

quiz.q: What did the Gemara conclude from the stories of the man saved from a lion and of Mar son of Ravina?
o: Only miracles for the many warrant a blessing
For a miracle of the many everyone blesses; for a miracle of an individual, the individual himself blesses
An individual blesses only once, not every time he passes the place
Miracles for individuals require a thanksgiving offering
quiz.e: Rava told the man to bless whenever he reached the spot, and Mar son of Ravina blessed at both sites of his rescues; the Sages concluded that an individual is obligated to bless for his own miracle.

quiz.q: Why does one recite 'the true Judge' at the site of Lot's wife, when the baraita speaks of thanks and praise?
o: Because Lot's wife was an idolater
Because Lot's wife is a tragedy; the baraita is emended so that one blesses 'the true Judge' for her and 'Who remembers the righteous' for Lot
Because the pillar of salt is a natural formation
Because no blessing is recited there at all
quiz.e: Since Lot's wife is a punishment, one says the True Judge; the baraita is read as requiring two blessings, the second recalling that even in His wrath God remembered Abraham and rescued Lot (Genesis 19:29).

quiz.q: How was Rav Yehuda's obligation to give thanks after his illness fulfilled, given Abaye's requirement of ten and the fact that he did not recite the blessing himself?
o: The Sages exempted him because he was a scholar
He brought a thanksgiving offering instead
Ten people were present, and by answering amen to their blessing he was considered to have blessed himself
The obligation applies only to seafarers and desert travelers
quiz.e: Rav Ḥana of Baghdad and the Sages blessed God for Rav Yehuda's recovery in the presence of ten, and his amen counted as his own thanksgiving.
